info.text:
When a neighbor wins the lottery, nearby bankruptcies tick up.
In Canadian data, a win equal to a year's median income (C$29,229) raised neighbors' bankruptcy rate 6.59% over three years, a relative rise on a low base (Philadelphia Fed working paper, 2018).
The bigger the win, the more visible stuff, like houses and cars, the bankrupt neighbors held.
In a 2011 Dutch study, next-door neighbors of lottery winners spent more on cars.
In a Bankrate survey (Aug 2023), social media impulse buyers spent an average of $754 in a year. Our math: over 10 years that's $7,540.
Sources: Agarwal, Mikhed & Scholnick (Philadelphia Fed, 2018); Kuhn et al. (American Economic Review, 2011); Bankrate (2023).
News and education, not financial advice.
